factsAccepted: Invoiced revenue grew 41% YoY to $14.2M, but net revenue is only $9.8M and true blended contribution margin fell from 19% to 11% over twelve months (-800bps) even as the top line accelerated. The divergence between invoiced growth and contribution decline indicates revenue is being bought with margin, not earned through profitable demand.

Channel contribution margins diverge sharply: DTC contribution is 44% while retail contribution is just 4%. Retail doors grew from 1,300 to 2,400 in twelve months — nearly all of the contribution erosion coincides with the door expansion, and the new doors are concentrated in the lower-velocity natural channel.

Trade spend has doubled from 9% to 18% of invoiced retail revenue in twelve months, refrigerated freight is $0.62/unit, and spoilage/short-code returns run 7% of retail shipments due to 90-day code life colliding with slow velocity in newer doors. There is no door-level velocity or SKU-level contribution reporting to attribute where the spend and spoilage are concentrated.

DTC subscriber base is flat at ~9,000 and DTC contribution remains strong at 44%, indicating brand demand and product quality are healthy where the brand controls economics. NPS and repeat rates on DTC are stable. The deterioration is therefore not a demand or product-quality problem; it tracks the shift in revenue mix toward subsidized retail distribution.
factsNeedingClarification: Door-level velocity: units sold per store per week (SPSW) by retailer and door cohort — needed to know which doors are below the breakeven velocity threshold
SKU-level true contribution after trade, freight, and spoilage — which of the 9 SKUs are margin-positive vs. negative
Channel-level fully-loaded P&L — true DTC vs. retail vs. Amazon contribution net of fulfillment, ad spend (CAC), and trade
Trade-spend ROI: lift per promotional dollar by retailer; whether promoted volume is incremental or merely subsidized base
Spoilage attribution: which doors/regions/SKUs generate short-code returns, and whether velocity or distribution overreach is the cause
